Another in the series: Beautiful Mars - Distant Peaks. Info in the 1st comment

Beautiful Mars - Distant Peaks

At the end of its drive on sol 1035 (July 07, 2015) the Hand Lens camera (MAHLI) acquired this single frame image. This camera is mounted to the turret at the end of the rover's robotic arm, so was parked during the drive, hence the rotation of the image. I have corrected that rotation. But the colours are left in the raw state as downlinked from JPL.

The peaks in the distance are the rim peaks of Gale crater. Gale crater has been the home of the rover since it landed, and are approximately 30 kilometers from the position of the rover currently at the entrance to Maria's Pass. The slopes on the left are the lower slopes of Mt Shields, beyond those slopes in the floor of Gale crater that extend all the way to the distant peaks of the crater rim.
